title: Energy-Efficient Large-Scale Vector Similarity Search in NAND-Flash via Hybrid Matching
problem: Vector similarity search (VSS) on large-scale datasets requires massive memory capacity and energy-intensive data transfers; existing in-memory search using NAND-based multi-bit content-addressable memory (MCAM) in approximate-search mode wastes energy comparing queries with non-target vectors.
motivation: AI workloads like few-shot learning and approximate nearest-neighbor search demand high-capacity, energy-efficient similarity search at scale.
method: Hybrid-M integrates exact-search (ES) and approximate-search (AS) modes in a single 3D NAND MCAM architecture: ES mode acts as a low-energy filter to eliminate non-target vectors before expensive AS-mode comparisons. Three optimization techniques: range encoding for multi-level cells (MLC) enhances filtering effectiveness; search voltage shifts reduce matching currents while maintaining AS accuracy; filtering-aware training improves reliability. The hybrid matching process selectively applies AS only to filtered candidates.
key_novelty: Dual-mode NAND-MCAM architecture that uses exact-search filtering to eliminate redundant approximate-search operations, reducing energy waste by orders of magnitude.
contributions: Hybrid matching approach combining ES and AS modes to reduce energy in VSS
Range encoding and voltage shift techniques to optimize MLC NAND for multi-mode operation
Filtering-aware training methodology to maintain accuracy and reliability
67-83% energy reduction across many-class FSL and ANNS workloads vs. AS-only approaches
limitations: Limited evaluation to specific FSL/ANNS benchmarks; scalability to mixed workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient in-memory vector similarity search via hybrid ES/AS filtering
